facts.value: gmTouSetup_UpdateEntrantTransitionAnimation
facts.rationale: Replaces the misleading TimeMenu hypothesis with the supported setup-to-entrant animation role; exact original spelling remains unknown.

evidence.why: Option-dependent animation refreshes entrant displays and selects state 10 at frame 49.

facts.value: Updates the Tournament setup model animation spanning the settings and entrant-configuration phases. It selects the applicable frame interval, refreshes entrant-list and selected-entrant text at transition frame 49, changes cur_option to 10, applies the current frame, and advances the shared byte counter.
facts.rationale: Corrects the unsupported time-selection interpretation while preserving the actual transition and animation operations.

evidence.why: Refresh modes 6 and 5 redraw entrant presentation.

facts.value: Provides the animated transition from Tournament Mode's settings phase into entrant configuration, together with the model's state-dependent idle animation. It is not specifically a time-selection interface.
facts.rationale: The transition enters the entrant state and refreshes entrant text; neither canonical behavior nor registration establishes a time-menu role.

evidence.why: Transition to state 10 and entrant-display refresh.
Registration in the Tournament setup presentation layer.

facts.value: For cur_option < 9, xE values above 39 reset to 10 before frame application, so the recurring applied frames are 10–39. For cur_option >= 9, xE == 49 refreshes modes 6 and 5 and sets cur_option to 10; values above 78 reset to 50 before application, yielding recurring frames 50–78. The applied value is incremented afterward, so stored values 40 and 79 are not applied on the following callback. Initial sequences are distinct from these loops: setup initializes xE to zero, and returning from entrant configuration also resets it to zero.
facts.rationale: Corrects the off-by-one applied-frame intervals and distinguishes initialization from steady looping.

facts.value: Reads shared TmData, the GObj's JObj root, cur_option, local handicap-enable and adjustment-enable fields, and the entrant selected by x2 + x3. The entrant's x2 handicap byte is applied as the hierarchy animation frame. Outputs include both animation-state changes and root/child visibility changes; the callback does not edit the entrant's handicap value.
facts.rationale: The previous explanation incorrectly limited outputs to visibility despite the explicit frame application.

evidence.why: Frame helper requests and evaluates animation.

facts.value: For match type zero, initialization derives active and human counts separately, converts handicap mode 1 to mode 0 with entrant handicap 9, optionally randomizes CPU levels, and performs 1000 swaps of entrant-order bytes. The shuffle excludes index zero when cached controller count lbl_804D665C is below two; this is not an early-round condition. Other match types use combatants for active and human counts, retain entrants in x30, and skip the shuffle. All 64 records receive character/costume defaults and active, human, CPU or inactive classification as applicable; local selection state is reset and cur_option becomes 9.
facts.rationale: Corrects the shuffle guard's meaning and preserves subtype-sensitive initialization.

evidence.why: Cached count producer for match type zero.

facts.value: Builds and resets Tournament Mode's setup interface and computes a 25-entry character-unlock cache used by entrant character presentation and input validation. The cache does not mean that every unavailable roster position disappears: downstream presentation and navigation retain distinct placeholder and eligibility branches.
facts.rationale: Corrects the claim that character-grid presentation is restricted exclusively to unlocked characters.

evidence.why: Navigation eligibility is broader than the unlock flag alone.

facts.value: tmSettings_HandleStageSelectionInput
facts.rationale: Dispatch index 4 edits stage_selection_type. This distinguishes the handler from the separate external rules-menu handoff.

facts.value: Handles Tournament setup's stage-selection-policy setting. Left/right input wraps the selected value using match-type-dependent bounds and requests display updates. A advances to CPU-level state 5 for match type zero or skips directly to setup-choice state 6 otherwise; B returns to composition state 3.
facts.rationale: Identifies the actual setting rather than conflating it with general custom-rules editing.

evidence.why: Complete handler and subtype-dependent next state.

facts.value: Implements the stage-selection-policy choice within Tournament Mode's sequential setup settings. It is distinct from the additional rules configuration interface opened by setup choice 7.
facts.rationale: Canonical field mapping and the separate handoff establish the distinction.

facts.value: gmTournament_HandleCpuLevelSetting
facts.rationale: Meaningfully narrows the generic SettingsInput name to the CPU-level field selected by dispatch state 5.

facts.value: Returns immediately for nonzero match type. Otherwise decrement takes precedence over increment, and A takes precedence over B. The step helpers wrap the CPU-level value using table bounds, play movement feedback and set x7 or x8 to five. A advances the option and B decrements it. Each nonzero input group requests display mode 3, preceded by mode 0 when the combined masks contain 0x100 or 0x200.
facts.rationale: Preserves input and refresh ordering while correcting the false no-timer assertion.

evidence.why: Step-helper bounds, sounds and timer writes.

facts.value: Consumes the current option and directional/action masks. Horizontal input changes the choice within 6–8. A or Start first invokes bracket-view teardown, then choice 6 initializes entrants, choice 7 sets TmData.x20 to one, resets SIS text, removes GObjs in inclusive link ranges 0x19–0x1C and 0x12–0x15, and passes MnExtAll with a subtype selector to the external rules menu; choice 8 returns to state zero. B selects state 5 for match type zero or state 4 otherwise. Qualifying input refreshes display mode zero.
facts.rationale: Corrects range configuration to object teardown and preserves the shared pause/resource handoff.

evidence.why: Range helper traverses and removes objects.

facts.value: Uses state_ptr as both cur_option and the enclosing TmData base. Local x2 + x3 selects the entrant; row and scroll changes refresh display modes 5 and 6. In enabled handicap-adjustment mode it edits entrant x2 between 1 and 9. A in states 10 or 12 snapshots current character, costume, special flag and name into backup fields x4, x8, x6 and the local overlay's u16 xB before entering the corresponding editor. Start saves the current option for final-confirmation cancellation. B either disables adjustment or returns to state 6, resets transition counter xE and conditionally rebuilds bracket presentation.
facts.rationale: Corrects backup direction and identifies the edited value as handicap while preserving indexing, overlay use and cancellation flow.

evidence.why: Character editor restores the snapshot fields on cancellation.

facts.value: Handles the Tournament entrant-list editor's character, name and handicap columns. It navigates the twelve-row window, opens character or name editing after saving cancellation backups, enables and performs bounded handicap adjustment, enters final confirmation on Start, and returns to setup choices on full cancellation.
facts.rationale: Replaces CPU-level editing and staged-commit claims with the supported handicap and editor-entry behavior.

evidence.why: Navigation, editor entry, handicap adjustment and exits.
Handicap x2 is initialized separately from CPU level x1.

facts.value: Implements Tournament Mode entrant-list navigation and access to character, saved-name and handicap customization for the active entrant pool, with a twelve-row scrolling view. The 1–9 value edited in state 16 is handicap, not computer-player level.
facts.rationale: Corrects the player-facing mechanic while retaining the entrant-configuration mapping.

evidence.why: Entrant navigation and state-16 value editing.

facts.value: Start has priority, saves the current option and enters state 17. Horizontal movement selects states 10, 12 and, when handicap is enabled, 16; leaving state 16 to the left clears adjustment flag x1. Vertical input normally navigates entrants through a twelve-row window, but in state 16 with x1 set it changes handicap within 1–9. A in state 10 or 12 saves cancellation backups and enters state 11 or 13. A in state 16 enables adjustment only when local handicap mode x0 is not 1. B clears active adjustment first; otherwise it returns to state 6, resets xE and rebuilds the bracket view for match type zero.
facts.rationale: Corrects confirmation terminology, backup semantics and the precise adjustment-enable guard.

facts.value: Handles the active Tournament entrant's character-selection step. It searches a wrapping five-by-five roster for eligible candidates, resets costume and special state after movement, steps costumes without wrapping, accepts an available character, and restores backups on B or before a Start-driven final-confirmation detour. A with held masks 0x40 and 0x20 in a nonzero match type sets the entrant's special-selection flag; the downstream interpretation of that flag is not established by this handler alone.
facts.rationale: Preserves the exceptional branch while avoiding unsupported randomization details and ambiguous costume-cycling wording.

evidence.why: Complete navigation, special confirmation, restoration and bounded costume logic.

facts.value: Implements Tournament entrant character selection through a five-by-five roster, availability-checked confirmation and bounded alternate-costume adjustment. It also exposes a subtype-specific held-button special-selection path; describing the eventual behavior as random character selection requires evidence from later consumers of the special flag.
facts.rationale: Limits the mapping to demonstrated behavior and preserves uncertainty about the downstream special-selection mechanic.

evidence.why: Roster interaction, availability checks, special flag and costume bounds.

facts.value: Selects the entrant with local x2 + x3 and the highlighted saved name with x5 + 4*x6. A snapshots the current name into the local overlay's u16 xB. State 13, when name storage has capacity, sets TmData.x20, resets SIS, removes interface objects in two link ranges and passes the retained MnExtAll archive to Name Entry. State 14 provisionally writes an occupied highlighted name, enters state 15 and redraws the name grid; final uniqueness validation occurs in fn_80195CCC. B restores the backup, refreshes entrant labels and returns to state 12.
facts.rationale: Corrects range teardown and distinguishes provisional assignment from later acceptance.

evidence.why: Source-choice input, snapshot, provisional assignment and handoff.
Later uniqueness acceptance and cancellation restoration.

facts.value: Handles the Tournament entrant's choice between creating a new saved name and opening the existing-name list. It saves the current assignment for cancellation, launches Name Entry when storage permits or initializes the list preview, restores the assignment on B, and supports a Start-driven detour to final confirmation. Opening the existing-name list is not final acceptance of its highlighted name.
facts.rationale: Corrects the prior claim that this source-choice screen accepts the highlighted existing name.

evidence.why: Actual existing-name acceptance is performed later.

facts.value: Start saves the current option, selects state 17 and returns before other input. Left changes 14 to 13 and right changes 13 to 14. A plays forward feedback and saves the current name: state 13 launches Name Entry only if fewer than 120 names exist, otherwise remains in place after the backup and sound; state 14 provisionally assigns the highlighted name only if GetNameText is non-null, then enters state 15 and redraws mode 4 regardless. B restores the backup, redraws modes 5 and 6 and selects state 12. Occupancy and uniqueness acceptance of an existing name belongs to the state-15 handler.
facts.rationale: Makes the full-capacity and empty-preview branches explicit and removes the premature commit interpretation.

facts.value: Rebuilds presentation, sets cur_option to zero and makes seven iterations requesting display modes 0, 2, 3 and 1 before incrementing the option, leaving it at 7. The display helper suppresses nonzero modes for option 6 at this stage. Only match type zero reconstructs the bracket view and applies the fixed overview camera parameters. Both paths clear x20 and set all 64 entrant x2 values to 5 when GameRules.handicap equals exactly 1, or to 9 otherwise.
facts.rationale: Preserves the initialization sequence while correcting the distinction between handicap mode 1 and arbitrary nonzero handicap modes, and clarifies the display helper's option-6 guard.

evidence.why: Seven iterations, subtype branch and exact handicap equality.
Option-6 suppression of nonzero display modes.
